function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **ready‑to‑run Bash script** that will:

1. Clone the repository (`git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`) into a temporary folder.  
2. Generate a minimal `Dockerfile`, a `k8s/deployment.yaml` + `k8s/service.yaml`, and a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`).  
3. Add the new files to the repo, commit them, and push the commit back to the remote.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have `git`, `docker`, and `kubectl` installed on the machine where you run this script.  
> * Your SSH key must already be added to your GitHub account so that `git@github.com` works without a password prompt.  
> * The script uses the default branch `main`. If your repo uses a different default branch, change the `BRANCH` variable accordingly.  

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# ---------- Configuration ----------
REPO_URL="git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git"
CLONE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"          # temporary directory for cloning
BRANCH="main"                     # default branch name
COMMIT_MSG="Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests & CI workflow"

# ---------- Step 1 – Clone the repo ----------
echo "Cloning $REPO_URL into $CLONE_DIR ..."
git clone --branch "$BRANCH" "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_DIR"

cd "$CLONE_DIR"

# ---------- Step 2 – Analyse the repo ----------
# For the purpose of this script we assume a typical Node.js layout:
#   - package.json (contains the start script)
#   - src/app.js (or index.js) – the entry point
#   - .gitignore (already present)
# If your repo has a different structure, adjust the paths below.

# ---------- Step 2.1 – Create/Update Dockerfile ----------
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
# Use official lightweight Node runtime
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package.json and package-lock.json first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the application code
COPY . .

# Expose the port that the app listens on (adjust if your app uses a different port)
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command to start the app
CMD ["npm", "start"]
EOF

echo "Dockerfile created."

# ---------- Step 2.2 – Create Kubernetes YAML files ----------
mkdir -p k8s

cat > k8s/deployment.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_DOCKER_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
EOF

cat > k8s/service.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer          # Change to ClusterIP / NodePort if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80                 # Service port exposed to the cluster
    targetPort: 3000         # Container port
EOF

echo "Kubernetes manifests created in k8s/"

# ---------- Step 2.3 – Create GitHub Actions workflow ----------
mkdir -p .github/workflows

cat > .github/workflows/ci.yml <<'EOF'
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]   # Adjust if your default branch is different

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout source
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        username: \${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
        password: \${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: \${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest

    - name: Deploy to Kubernetes
      uses: azure/k8s-deploy@v4
      with:
        manifests: |
          k8s/deployment.yaml
          k8s/service.yaml
        images: |
          \${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
        kubeconfig: \${{ secrets.KUBECONFIG }}   # Store your kubeconfig as a secret
EOF

echo "GitHub Actions workflow created at .github/workflows/ci.yml"

# ---------- Step 3 – Add all changed files to git ----------
git add Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# ---------- Step 4 – Commit and push ----------
git commit -m "$COMMIT_MSG"
git push origin "$BRANCH"

echo "All changes committed and pushed to $REPO_URL on branch $BRANCH."
```

### How to run the script

1. Save the script above to a file, e.g. `setup.sh`.  
2. Make it executable:  
   ```bash
   chmod +x setup.sh
   ```  
3. Run it:  
   ```bash
   ./setup.sh
   ```

The script will automatically clone the repo, generate the required files, commit them, and push the commit back to the remote.  

> **Important notes**  
> * Replace `<YOUR_DOCKER_REGISTRY>` in `k8s/deployment.yaml` with the actual registry you intend to use (e.g., `ghcr.io/zelarhq`).  
> * The GitHub Actions workflow expects the following secrets to be defined in the repository settings:  
>   - `DOCKER_USERNAME` – your Docker registry username  
>   - `DOCKER_PASSWORD` – your Docker registry password or token  
>   - `KUBECONFIG` – a base64‑encoded kubeconfig file that allows the workflow to deploy to your cluster.  
> * If your Node.js app listens on a port other than `3000`, update the `EXPOSE` line in the Dockerfile and the `containerPort`/`targetPort` values in the Kubernetes manifests accordingly.  

Feel free to tweak the generated files to better fit your application's specifics. Happy coding!
